s121.content:
The eldest son of an Italian marquis, Aloysius renounced his inheritance to join the Jesuits, overcoming his father’s fierce opposition. He was known for his purity and his intense prayer.

When plague struck Rome in 1591, he volunteered to care for the sick, carrying the dying to the hospital. He caught the disease and died at 23. He is a patron of youth and of students.
s121.intercession: St. Aloysius, pray for all young people. Help them to live pure and generous lives, and to give themselves wholeheartedly to the service of God and neighbor. Amen.

s122.content:
A lawyer turned priest, Francis de Sales won thousands back to the Catholic faith in the Calvinist Chablais region, partly by slipping pamphlets under doors. As bishop of Geneva he was known for his gentleness.

His Introduction to the Devout Life taught that holiness is possible for people in every walk of life. With St. Jane Frances de Chantal he founded the Visitation order. He is the patron of writers and journalists.
s122.intercession: St. Francis de Sales, gentle teacher of devotion, pray for us. Help us to seek holiness in our daily duties and to speak the truth with patience and love. Amen.

s123.content:
A French baroness widowed at 28 with four children, Jane placed herself under the spiritual direction of St. Francis de Sales. Together they founded the Order of the Visitation of Holy Mary in 1610 for women whose health or age barred them from stricter orders.

She endured the loss of many loved ones and long periods of spiritual darkness, yet founded more than eighty convents. She is a patron of widows and of parents separated from their children.
s123.intercession: St. Jane Frances de Chantal, pray for widows and all who grieve. Help us to hold fast to God in times of loss and spiritual dryness. Amen.

s124.content:
Paul Miki, a Japanese Jesuit and gifted preacher, was one of 26 Catholics crucified on a hill at Nagasaki in 1597 on the orders of the ruler Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The group included priests, brothers, catechists, and boys as young as twelve.

From the cross, Paul preached to the crowd and forgave his executioners. Japanese Christians later kept the faith in secret for more than two centuries without priests.
s124.intercession: St. Paul Miki and companions, pray for all persecuted Christians. Give them courage to witness to Christ and the grace to forgive. Amen.

s125.content:
A Filipino husband and father of Chinese descent, Lorenzo worked as a calligrapher in Manila. Falsely accused of a crime, he fled aboard a ship carrying Dominican missionaries to Japan, where Christianity was banned.

Arrested and tortured in Nagasaki, he refused to renounce his faith, declaring that he would die for God a thousand times. Canonized in 1987, he is the first Filipino saint.
s125.intercession: St. Lorenzo Ruiz, pray for the Filipino people and for all migrants. Give us the faith to say, whatever the cost: I am a Christian. Amen.

s126.content:
Considered slow-witted and clumsy as a youth, Joseph was turned away by several religious orders before the Franciscans accepted him. He barely passed his exams for ordination, answering the only questions he had studied.

He became famous for ecstasies during prayer, when he was reportedly seen rising into the air. He is the patron of students taking exams and of pilots and air travelers.
s126.intercession: St. Joseph of Cupertino, pray for all students, especially those facing exams. Help us to do our best, to trust God with the rest, and to be lifted up in prayer. Amen.

s127.content:
The North American Martyrs were six French Jesuits and two lay helpers killed while working among the Huron and Iroquois peoples in what is now Canada and New York. Isaac Jogues was captured, tortured, and mutilated in 1642, escaped to France, and then chose to return.

He was killed at Ossernenon, near present-day Auriesville, New York, in 1646. St. Kateri Tekakwitha was born in the same village a decade later.
s127.intercession: St. Isaac Jogues and companions, pray for us. Give missionaries perseverance and courage, and help us to return to our duty even after we have suffered. Amen.

s128.content:
A Visitation nun at Paray-le-Monial in France, Margaret Mary received a series of visions of Christ between 1673 and 1675. He showed her his Heart, burning with love for humanity, and asked for a feast of the Sacred Heart and devotion on the First Fridays.

She met doubt and hostility, but with the support of St. Claude de la Colombière, devotion to the Sacred Heart spread throughout the Church.
s128.intercession: St. Margaret Mary, apostle of the Sacred Heart, pray for us. Help us to trust in the love of Jesus and to make reparation for the coldness of the world. Amen.

s129.content:
A French priest who preached missions across western France, Louis de Montfort was known for his poverty, his fiery preaching, and his love of the Rosary. He founded the Company of Mary and the Daughters of Wisdom.

His True Devotion to Mary, lost after his death and rediscovered in 1842, teaches total consecration to Jesus through Mary. It deeply influenced Pope John Paul II, whose motto Totus Tuus came from it.
s129.intercession: St. Louis de Montfort, pray for us. Lead us to Jesus through Mary, and help us to give ourselves totally to him. Amen.

s130.content:
The son of a poor tailor in southern Italy, Gerard was turned away by the Capuchins for poor health before becoming a Redemptorist lay brother. He worked as a tailor, sacristan, and porter and was known for his obedience and for many reported miracles.

Shortly before his death, he left his handkerchief with a family; a woman in their family later used it during a dangerous childbirth and delivered safely. He is the patron of expectant mothers.
s130.intercession: St. Gerard Majella, pray for all expectant mothers and their children. Give them safe deliveries and healthy babies, and comfort all who long for a child. Amen.

s131.content:
A Franciscan professor from Mallorca, Junípero Serra gave up an academic career to serve in the missions of New Spain. Despite a chronically injured leg, he walked thousands of miles and founded nine of the California missions, beginning with San Diego in 1769.

His legacy is debated because of the mission system’s effects on Native peoples. Pope Francis canonized him in 2015 in Washington, D.C., the first canonization on U.S. soil.
s131.intercession: St. Junípero Serra, pray for us. Give us missionary zeal, and help the Church to proclaim the Gospel with respect for the dignity of every people. Amen.

s132.content:
Rejected by several monasteries, Benedict Joseph Labre felt called to a life of pilgrimage. For years he walked to shrines across Europe, living as a beggar, often sharing the alms he received.

He settled in Rome, sleeping in the ruins of the Colosseum and praying for hours in churches. He collapsed and died during Holy Week at 35. He is a patron of homeless people.
s132.intercession: St. Benedict Joseph Labre, pray for all who are homeless. Help us to see them as our brothers and sisters and to treat them with dignity and love. Amen.

s133.content:
Born in Bohemia, John Neumann came to New York in 1836 and was ordained there. He joined the Redemptorists and served German immigrants before becoming bishop of Philadelphia in 1852.

He built dozens of churches and organized the first diocesan Catholic school system in the United States. He was the first American bishop canonized, in 1977.
s133.intercession: St. John Neumann, friend of immigrants, pray for us. Help us to welcome newcomers and to give children a sound education in faith. Amen.

s134.content:
A farmer’s daughter who joined the Daughters of Charity, Catherine received visions of the Virgin Mary in 1830 at their chapel on the Rue du Bac in Paris. Mary asked her to have a medal struck with the words "O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee."

The Miraculous Medal spread quickly around the world. Catherine revealed her identity only shortly before her death, having spent 46 years quietly caring for elderly men. Her body remains incorrupt.
s134.intercession: St. Catherine Labouré, pray for us. Help us to trust Our Lady’s care and to serve God faithfully in hidden, ordinary work. Amen.

s135.content:
Korean Catholicism began in the 1780s among lay scholars who read Christian books, without missionaries. Andrew Kim Taegon, the son of converts, studied in Macau and became the first Korean-born priest in 1845.

He was beheaded near Seoul in 1846 at age 25. He is honored with 102 other Korean martyrs killed between 1839 and 1867, whom Pope John Paul II canonized in Seoul in 1984.
s135.intercession: St. Andrew Kim Taegon and companions, pray for the Church in Korea and wherever the faith is persecuted. Help us to treasure the gift of faith. Amen.

s136.content:
Charles Lwanga was the head of the royal pages at the court of King Mwanga II of Buganda (in present-day Uganda). When the king turned against Christians, Charles secretly baptized several of the young pages in his care and protected them from the king’s abuse.

On June 3, 1886, he and many companions were burned alive at Namugongo. The 22 Catholic martyrs were canonized in 1964. Their shrine draws millions of pilgrims every year.
s136.intercession: St. Charles Lwanga and companions, pray for the Church in Africa and for all young people. Give them courage to protect the vulnerable and to stay pure. Amen.

s137.content:
An Anglican priest and Oxford scholar, Newman was a leader of the Oxford Movement before his study of the early Church led him to become Catholic in 1845. He founded the Oratory in England and wrote The Idea of a University and the autobiography Apologia Pro Vita Sua.

He was made a cardinal in 1879, taking the motto "Heart speaks to heart." Canonized in 2019, he was declared a Doctor of the Church in 2025 and named co-patron of Catholic education.
s137.intercession: St. John Henry Newman, pray for all who seek the truth. Lead us, kindly Light, amid the encircling gloom, and help heart to speak to heart. Amen.

s138.content:
Louis, a watchmaker, and Zélie, a lacemaker, married in Alençon in 1858. They had nine children, four of whom died young. All five surviving daughters became nuns, including St. Thérèse of Lisieux.

Zélie died of breast cancer in 1877. Louis later suffered from a debilitating illness. Canonized together in 2015, they were the first married couple canonized in the same ceremony.
s138.intercession: Sts. Louis and Zélie Martin, pray for all married couples and families. Help parents to raise their children in faith and to bear suffering together with love. Amen.

s139.content:
A Maronite monk from Lebanon, Charbel lived the last 23 years of his life as a hermit, dedicated to prayer, fasting, and the celebration of the Divine Liturgy.

After his death, light was reported around his tomb and his body was found incorrupt. Thousands of healings have been attributed to his intercession, and he is venerated by both Christians and Muslims. He was canonized in 1977.
s139.intercession: St. Charbel, man of silence and prayer, pray for us and for the people of Lebanon and the Middle East. Obtain healing for the sick and peace for the troubled. Amen.

s140.content:
A German-born Franciscan sister from Syracuse, New York, Marianne Cope helped found two hospitals before answering a call to serve leprosy patients in Hawaii in 1883.

She cared for St. Damien of Molokai in his final illness and took over his work at Kalaupapa, where she served for thirty years without contracting the disease. She was canonized in 2012.
s140.intercession: St. Marianne Cope, pray for the sick and all who serve them. Help us to care for the outcast with courage and joy. Amen.

s141.content:
The son of a poor postman, Giuseppe Sarto served as a parish priest, bishop of Mantua, and patriarch of Venice before his election as pope in 1903. His motto was "to restore all things in Christ."

He encouraged frequent Communion, lowered the age of First Communion to about seven, promoted Gregorian chant, and began the codification of canon law. He was canonized in 1954.
s141.intercession: Pope St. Pius X, pray for us. Help us to restore all things in Christ and to receive him often and worthily in the Eucharist. Amen.

s142.content:
Heiress to a Philadelphia banking fortune, Katharine Drexel asked Pope Leo XIII to send missionaries to Native Americans. He suggested she become one herself.

In 1891 she founded the Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament to serve Native American and Black communities and spent her fortune founding schools, including Xavier University of Louisiana. She was canonized in 2000.
s142.intercession: St. Katharine Drexel, pray for us. Help us to use our gifts in the service of justice and to work for the dignity of every person. Amen.

s143.content:
The daughter of poor farmworkers near Rome, Maria Goretti was eleven when a neighbor, Alessandro Serenelli, tried to rape her. She resisted and he stabbed her fourteen times. Before she died the next day, she forgave him.

After years in prison, Alessandro repented and later begged Maria’s mother for forgiveness. He attended Maria’s canonization in 1950 and spent his last years as a lay brother with the Capuchins.
s143.intercession: St. Maria Goretti, pray for us. Help young people to value purity and all of us to forgive those who have hurt us most. Amen.

s144.content:
An Italian orphan who suffered from poor health and was prevented from entering religious life, Gemma lived a hidden life of prayer in Lucca. She is said to have received the stigmata and experienced frequent ecstasies.

She offered her many sufferings in union with Christ’s Passion and died of tuberculosis at 25. She is a patron of pharmacists and of those suffering from back pain.
s144.intercession: St. Gemma Galgani, pray for us. Help us to unite our sufferings to the Passion of Jesus and to love him with a pure heart. Amen.

s145.content:
Mary MacKillop co-founded the Sisters of St. Joseph of the Sacred Heart in 1866 to educate poor children in the Australian countryside. Her sisters went wherever families lived, including remote areas.

After a dispute with a local bishop, she was briefly excommunicated in 1871; the decision was reversed months later. She was canonized in 2010 as Australia’s first saint.
s145.intercession: St. Mary MacKillop, pray for us. Help us to never see a need without doing something about it, and to trust God through misunderstanding. Amen.

s146.content:
A physician, researcher, and professor in Naples, Giuseppe Moscati treated the poor for free and often slipped money into prescriptions for those who could not afford medicine. He attended daily Mass and saw his work as a ministry.

During the 1906 eruption of Vesuvius he helped evacuate a hospital before its roof collapsed. He was canonized in 1987, one of the first modern physicians to be declared a saint.
s146.intercession: St. Giuseppe Moscati, holy physician, pray for all doctors and patients. Help medical professionals to serve with skill, faith, and compassion. Amen.

s147.content:
Siblings from Aljustrel, Portugal, Francisco and Jacinta and their cousin Lúcia saw the Virgin Mary six times at Fatima in 1917. She asked them to pray the Rosary and do penance for sinners.

Both died young in the influenza pandemic. Francisco wanted to console Jesus, and Jacinta offered her suffering for sinners. Canonized in 2017, they are the youngest non-martyrs ever canonized.
s147.intercession: Sts. Francisco and Jacinta, pray for all children and for the conversion of sinners. Help us to pray the Rosary faithfully and to console the Heart of Jesus. Amen.

s148.content:
Born into a Jewish family in Breslau, Edith Stein became a philosopher and a student of Edmund Husserl. After reading the autobiography of St. Teresa of Ávila in one night, she became Catholic in 1922 and later entered the Carmelites.

She was arrested by the Nazis in the Netherlands in 1942 and killed at Auschwitz. She was canonized in 1998 and named a co-patron of Europe in 1999.
s148.intercession: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross, pray for us. Help us to seek truth with honesty and to embrace the Cross with love for all peoples. Amen.

s149.content:
The son of a wealthy Turin newspaper owner, Pier Giorgio loved mountain climbing, jokes, and friends, and he quietly spent his allowance on the poor. He was active in Catholic Action and the St. Vincent de Paul Society.

He died at 24 of polio, probably contracted while visiting the sick. Thousands of the poor he had helped came to his funeral. His motto was "Verso l’alto," "To the heights." He was canonized in 2025.
s149.intercession: St. Pier Giorgio Frassati, pray for young people. Help them to live joyfully, to serve the poor, and to climb always toward the heights. Amen.

s150.content:
Angelo Roncalli was one of thirteen children of a farming family near Bergamo. As a papal diplomat in Bulgaria, Turkey, and France, he helped Jews escape the Holocaust.

Elected pope in 1958 at 76, he surprised the world by calling the Second Vatican Council. His encyclical Pacem in Terris addressed all people of goodwill. Called "the Good Pope," he was canonized in 2014.
s150.intercession: Pope St. John XXIII, pray for the Church and for peace in the world. Give us your warmth, your humor, and your openness to the Holy Spirit. Amen.

s151.content:
A Spanish priest, Josemaría Escrivá founded Opus Dei in 1928 to spread the message that ordinary work and daily life can be a path to holiness.

During the Spanish Civil War he hid and later escaped across the Pyrenees. His books, such as The Way, have sold millions of copies. He was canonized in 2002.
s151.intercession: St. Josemaría, pray for us. Help us to sanctify our work and to find God in the ordinary circumstances of everyday life. Amen.

s152.content:
Giovanni Battista Montini served in the Vatican Secretariat of State and as archbishop of Milan before his election in 1963. He brought the Second Vatican Council to its conclusion and implemented its reforms.

He was the first pope to travel by plane to other continents and wrote Humanae Vitae, Populorum Progressio, and Evangelii Nuntiandi. He was canonized in 2018.
s152.intercession: Pope St. Paul VI, pray for the Church. Give her courage to proclaim the Gospel in every culture and to defend the dignity of human life. Amen.

s153.content:
Initially seen as a cautious conservative, Óscar Romero became archbishop of San Salvador in 1977. The murder of his friend, the Jesuit Rutilio Grande, changed him, and he began speaking out against the violence and repression afflicting El Salvador.

In his radio homilies he pleaded with soldiers to stop killing. He was shot dead while celebrating Mass on March 24, 1980. He was canonized in 2018.
s153.intercession: St. Óscar Romero, voice of the voiceless, pray for us. Give us courage to defend the poor and to speak the truth in love. Amen.

s154.content:
A London-born Italian teenager, Carlo Acutis loved video games, soccer, and computers, and he taught himself to code. He attended Mass daily and called the Eucharist "my highway to heaven."

He built a website cataloguing Eucharistic miracles around the world, which has been shown in many countries. He died of leukemia at fifteen, offering his suffering for the Pope and the Church. Canonized in 2025, he is the first millennial saint.
s154.intercession: St. Carlo Acutis, pray for young people. Help us to use technology for good and to make the Eucharist the center of our lives. Amen.

s155.content:
Gabriel, whose name means "strength of God," appears in Scripture as God’s messenger. He explained visions to the prophet Daniel, announced the birth of John the Baptist to Zechariah, and announced to Mary that she would conceive the Son of God.

His greeting "Hail, full of grace" forms the opening of the Hail Mary. He is the patron of messengers, telecommunications workers, and broadcasters.
s155.intercession: St. Gabriel the Archangel, messenger of the Incarnation, pray for us. Help us to hear God’s word and, like Mary, to answer: let it be to me according to your word. Amen.

s156.content:
Raphael, whose name means "God heals," appears in the Book of Tobit, where he guides young Tobias on a journey, helps him find a wife, and heals his father’s blindness. Only at the end does he reveal himself as "one of the seven holy angels who present the prayers of the saints and enter into the presence of the glory of the Holy One."

He is a patron of travelers, of the sick, of doctors and nurses, and of those seeking a spouse.
s156.intercession: St. Raphael the Archangel, pray for us. Guide us on our journeys, bring healing to the sick, and lead those seeking a spouse to one who will help them to God. Amen.

s157.content:
After the death of Judas, the eleven apostles prayed and cast lots to choose a replacement from among those who had followed Jesus from his baptism to his Ascension. The lot fell to Matthias, who was numbered with the Twelve (Acts 1).

Tradition says he preached in Judea and later in Cappadocia or Ethiopia, where he died a martyr. He reminds us that God calls quietly faithful disciples to great responsibility.
s157.intercession: St. Matthias, chosen to take the place of one who fell away, pray for us. Help us to remain faithful disciples and to answer God’s call whenever it comes. Amen.

s158.content:
Philip of Bethsaida was among the first called by Jesus, and he immediately brought his friend Nathanael with the words "Come and see." At the feeding of the five thousand and at the Last Supper, his honest questions drew some of Jesus’ most important teaching.

Tradition holds that he preached in Greece and Asia Minor and was martyred at Hierapolis. He shares his feast with St. James the Less.
s158.intercession: St. Philip, who brought your friend to Jesus, pray for us. Give us the courage to invite others to come and see the Lord, and to ask Him our honest questions. Amen.

s159.content:
James, son of Alphaeus, was one of the Twelve. Tradition long identified him with "James, the brother of the Lord," who led the church in Jerusalem, spoke at the Council of Jerusalem, and is honored as the author of the Letter of James.

According to the historian Josephus, James of Jerusalem was stoned to death around the year 62. He is remembered for his prayer, his justice, and his insistence that faith must show itself in works.
s159.intercession: St. James, pray for us. Help us to be doers of the word and not hearers only, so that our faith may bear fruit in love. Amen.

s160.content:
Simon is named in every list of the Twelve, called "the Zealot" perhaps for his zeal for the Law or for his former ties to a movement that resisted Roman rule. Nothing else about him is recorded in the Gospels.

Tradition says he preached in Egypt and Persia alongside St. Jude, with whom he shares a feast day, and that both were martyred there. He shows how Christ gathers people of every background into one family.
s160.intercession: St. Simon, whose zeal was turned to the service of Christ, pray for us. Direct our passions toward the Kingdom of God. Amen.
